# CFF test fonts

Small OpenType CFF fonts for the host tests of the TrueType/CFF engine (`lib/EpdFont/ttf/`). The CFF rasterizer
is checked byte-for-byte against FreeType's CFF driver, which the host oracle (`test/ttf_rasterizer`) compiles in.
Every file here is generated by `lib/EpdFont/scripts/make_cff_fixtures.py`; do not edit them by hand.

| Font | What it is | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NotoSansJP-Cff.otf`, `NotoSerifJP-Cff.otf` | CID-keyed subsets of Noto Sans / Serif CJK JP Regular, subroutines kept | the CID-keyed path: FDSelect, per-FD Private dicts, local and global subroutines |
| `NotoSansJP-CffFlat.otf`, `NotoSerifJP-CffFlat.otf` | the same subsets with every subroutine inlined (`desubroutinize()`) | outlines without subroutine calls, to tell a subroutine fault from an operator fault |
| `NotoSansJP-CffSlanted.otf` | `NotoSansJP-CffFlat` with the top DICT FontMatrix `[0.001 0 0.0002 0.001 0 0]` | a non-identity FontMatrix |
| `NotoSansJP-TrueType.ttf` | `NotoSansJP-CffFlat` as TrueType: each cubic turned into quadratics within one font unit (fontTools' `Cu2QuPen`) | the device bench's run of the same characters as CFF and as TrueType (`bench/ttf_raster_main.cpp`) |
| `CffOperators.otf` | a name-keyed font, one glyph per Type 2 operator family | every operator, hintmask/cntrmask with 8 and 9 stems, seac, subroutines nested 15 deep |
| `NotoSansDevanagari-Shaping-Regular.ttf`, `-Bold.ttf` | TrueType subsets of Noto Sans Devanagari holding the code points of 16 Devanagari words (conjuncts, reph, matras, nukta, ZWJ, Marathi and Nepali forms) plus U+0020, U+200C, U+200D and U+25CC; unhinted, GDEF, GSUB and GPOS kept whole, each under 64 KB | step 2 PR 2's shaping tests: `OtShaperReference.TheTrueTypeSubsetShapesAsHarfBuzz` checks `lib/OtShaper` against HarfBuzz's runs for them (`test/ttf_font/ExpectedGlyphRuns.h`) |
| `NotoSansDevanagari-Book-Regular.ttf`, `NotoSansBengali-Book-Regular.ttf`, `NotoSansTamil-Book-Regular.ttf`, `NotoSansMalayalam-Book-Regular.ttf` | TrueType subsets of the unhinted Noto Sans Regular of each script, holding the code points of its book's XHTML (`test/epubs/test_shaped_<script>.epub`) plus U+0020, U+200C, U+200D and U+25CC, the Devanagari one also the Devanagari code points of `test/epubs/test_shaped_bidi_indic.epub` (none it lacked: its Hindi words are the Hindi book's); GDEF, GSUB and GPOS kept whole, each under 128 KB | the shaped-Indic books, and the Hebrew book with Hindi words (the Devanagari one): each is laid out with its font as the shaping face of every font and style, for its `EpubPipelineTest` golden and `ShapingRulesTest`'s rules |
| `NotoNaskhArabic-Book-Regular.ttf` | a TrueType subset of Noto Naskh Arabic Regular merged with Noto Serif's Latin by `lib/EpdFont/scripts/merge_noto_latin.py` (as the Font Manager's NotoNaskhArabic family is merged), holding the code points of the three Arabic-script books' XHTML (`test/epubs/test_shaped_arabic.epub`, `test_shaped_persian.epub`, `test_shaped_urdu.epub`) plus U+0020, U+200C, U+200D, U+25CC and U+0640; GDEF, GSUB and GPOS kept whole, 45,568 B (under 128 KB) | the shaped Arabic-script books, as the Indic ones: their goldens, `ShapingRulesTest`'s rules, and `BidiRulesTest`'s Arabic cases |
| `NotoSansMyanmar-Book-Regular.ttf` | a TrueType subset of Noto Sans Myanmar Regular merged with Noto Sans's Latin by `lib/EpdFont/scripts/merge_noto_latin.py` (as the Font Manager's NotoSansMyanmar family is merged), holding the code points of the Myanmar book's XHTML (`test/epubs/test_shaped_myanmar.epub`: Burmese, Mon and Shan) plus U+0020, U+200C, U+200D and U+25CC; GDEF, GSUB and GPOS kept whole, 81,760 B (under 128 KB) | the shaped Myanmar book, as the Indic ones: its golden and `ShapingRulesTest`'s rules |
| `NotoNaskhArabic-Shaping-Regular.ttf`, `NotoSansArabic-Shaping-Bold.ttf` | TrueType subsets of the merged Arabic families (Noto Naskh Arabic Regular with Noto Serif's Latin, Noto Sans Arabic Bold with Noto Sans's, by `lib/EpdFont/scripts/merge_noto_latin.py`), cut to the code points of the Arabic test words (every Arabic letter of U+0621-064A, 066E-066F, 0671-06D3, 06D5, 06EE-06EF, 06FA-06FC, 06FF and 0750-077F both fonts map, in its four joining positions next to beh; lam-alef, harakat, shadda and the modifier marks in both orders, ZWNJ/ZWJ, tatweel, Persian, Urdu and Sindhi letters, digits) plus U+0020, U+200C, U+200D, U+25CC, `A` and `a`; unhinted, GDEF, GSUB and GPOS kept whole | step 2 PR 4a: the Arabic plan and shaper tests check `lib/OtShaper` against HarfBuzz's planned lookups and glyph runs for them (`test/ot_shaper/ArabicExpected.h`) |
| `NotoNaskhArabic-Numbers-Regular.ttf` | a TrueType subset of the Font Manager's NotoNaskhArabic Regular (`assets/sd-fonts/NotoNaskhArabic`, its sha256 checked), cut by `test/ot_shaper/make_arabic_number_fixtures.py` to the Arabic number signs (U+0600-0605, 06DD, 0890-0891, 08E2), the three digit sets (U+0030-0039, 0660-0669, 06F0-06F9), beh and U+0020; GDEF, GSUB and GPOS kept whole, 18,728 B | the number runs: `IndicShaper`'s and `ShapedLayout`'s number-sign tests check the sign drawn around its digits against HarfBuzz's runs (`test/ot_shaper/ArabicNumberExpected.h`) |
| `NotoSansMyanmar-Shaping-Regular.ttf` | a TrueType subset of Noto Sans Myanmar Regular (unhinted, not merged), cut to the code points of the Myanmar test words (pre-base vowel, medial ra, kinzi, stacks, dotted circles, dot below and asat, Mon, Shan and Karen signs, digits, joiners; Somnius/CrossInk-Indic's test words among them) plus U+0020, U+200C, U+200D and U+25CC; GDEF, GSUB and GPOS kept whole, 32,976 B | the Myanmar design's PR 1: `OtMyanmarTest` checks `lib/OtShaper`'s Myanmar shaper against HarfBuzz's planned lookups and glyph runs for it (`test/ot_shaper/MyanmarExpected.h`) |
| `NotoSansGrantha-Kern-Regular.ttf` | a TrueType subset of Noto Sans Grantha 2.001 (unhinted, notofonts/noto-fonts), holding sha (U+11336), the anusvara (U+11302) and U+0020; every layout feature kept, 2,824 B. Its 'kern' feature's pair adjustment lookup sets LookupFlag 0x0508 (IgnoreMarks, mark attachment class 5) and kerns sha before the anusvara, a mark, by -40 units | GDEF-aware kerning: a real font whose pair HarfBuzz does not kern (0 against -40 before), and whose family identity therefore changes once (`ttf::kernsByGdefClass`) |
| `ArabicRtlTest-Regular.ttf` | a synthetic 25-glyph font, this repository's own data (`fontTools.fontBuilder` and `feaLib`): `curs` with and without the RightToLeft lookup flag, `isol`/`init`/`medi`/`fina`, the lam-alef `rlig`, `calt` under a `dflt` language system without `rclt` and a `URD` one with it, mark to base and mark to mark, `ccmp`; U+0627 and U+0653 mapped, U+0622 left unmapped | what neither Noto family has: the plan's stages with and without `rclt`, cursive attachment in both directions, the normalizer's decomposition of an unmapped U+0622 |

The Noto subsets hold ASCII U+0020-007E, the marks `、。「」・ー`, hiragana U+3041-3093, katakana U+30A1-30F3 and the
kanji `日本語文字書読鬱慶議驚龍鑑響漢点線曲円角` (288 glyphs each). They are subset without hinting, with the `kern`
layout feature only. `TtfEmboldenTest` reads the dense kanji 鬱書慶議驚 of `NotoSansJP-TrueType.ttf`,
`NotoSansJP-Cff.otf` and `NotoSerifJP-Cff.otf` (synthetic bold's counters, spec 7.2).

`CffOperators.otf` ("CFF Operators Test") is this repository's own test data, written by the script with fontTools'
`FontBuilder`; it contains no third-party data. It has no glyph using `random` (FreeType's result for it is not
reproducible). Its bounding boxes are fixed values, since fontTools cannot trace the arithmetic operators.

## Regenerating

Download the two sources into one directory, then, from the repository root:

    python lib/EpdFont/scripts/make_cff_fixtures.py --source-dir <dir with the two OTFs> --out test/fixtures/fonts

The script checks both sha256 values (it does not download) and writes only the seven fonts. The output is
byte-identical on every run; `git status --short test/fixtures` shows no change after a second run. Needs
`fonttools`.

The Devanagari subsets and their expected HarfBuzz runs come from `lib/EpdFont/scripts/make_shaping_fixtures.py`.
Download the two Noto Sans Devanagari TTFs into one directory, then, from the repository root:

    python lib/EpdFont/scripts/make_shaping_fixtures.py --source-dir <dir with the two TTFs> --fonts-out test/fixtures/fonts --header-out test/ttf_font/ExpectedGlyphRuns.h

It checks both sha256 values (it does not download), writes the two subsets and the header, and is byte-identical on
every run. Needs `fonttools` and `uharfbuzz`. The words, the conversion and `round_px` are crosspoint-reader PR #3787's
`generate_fixtures.py` (SSafayet / @SSafayet).

The shaped-book subsets come from `lib/EpdFont/scripts/make_shaped_book_fonts.py`, from the books, so regenerate the
books first when their text changes (`python -I test/epubs/make_test_shaped_indic.py` and
`python -I test/epubs/make_test_shaped_arabic.py`). Download the four Noto Sans Regular TTFs (Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil,
Malayalam), Noto Naskh Arabic Regular and Noto Serif Regular (the Sources table) into one directory, then, from the
repository root:

    python lib/EpdFont/scripts/make_shaped_book_fonts.py --source-dir <dir with the six TTFs> --books test/epubs --fonts-out test/fixtures/fonts

It checks the six sha256 values (it does not download), merges Noto Serif's Latin into Noto Naskh Arabic, fails a font
of 131,072 bytes or more, writes only the five fonts, and is byte-identical on every run. Needs `fonttools` 4.63.0 (the
merge's bytes depend on it).

The Arabic fixtures and their expected HarfBuzz answers come from `test/ot_shaper/make_arabic_fixtures.py`. Download the four
Noto TTFs of the Sources table (Noto Naskh Arabic Regular, Noto Serif Regular, Noto Sans Arabic Bold, Noto Sans Bold) into one
directory, then, from the repository root:

    python -I test/ot_shaper/make_arabic_fixtures.py <dir with the four TTFs> test/fixtures/fonts

It checks the four sha256 values (it does not download), writes the three fonts and `test/ot_shaper/ArabicExpected.h`
(HarfBuzz's planned lookups and glyph runs, right to left, script Arab, scale 2133, ppem 33), and is byte-identical on every
run. Needs `fonttools` 4.63.0 and `uharfbuzz` 0.56.2.

The Myanmar fixture and its expected HarfBuzz answers come from `test/ot_shaper/make_myanmar_fixtures.py`. Download
Noto Sans Myanmar Regular (the Sources table) into a directory, then, from the repository root:

    python -I test/ot_shaper/make_myanmar_fixtures.py <dir with the TTF> test/fixtures/fonts

It checks the sha256 value (it does not download), writes the font and `test/ot_shaper/MyanmarExpected.h` (HarfBuzz's
planned lookups and glyph runs, left to right, script Mymr, scale 2133, ppem 33), and is byte-identical on every run.
Needs `fonttools` 4.63.0 and `uharfbuzz` 0.56.2.
